intro: A quiet Sunday for news overall. The big themes are AI tools hiding or replacing clicks (Gemini dropping link tags, Alexa shopping) and platforms paying creators.

must_reads.title: Google Gemini drops UTM tags from cited links after three weeks
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Gemini briefly tagged the links it cites, then quietly stopped, so those visits now show up as 'Direct' in analytics. When AI tools hide where clicks come from, knowing which link actually drove a visit or sale gets harder for everyone, and that's the problem smart links exist to solve.

must_reads.title: Amazon says more than 400M customers have used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Amazon says 400M+ people used Alexa for Shopping in a year and they spend 50% more. Shopping is moving into voice and AI assistants where nobody clicks a creator's link, which raises a real question about how creators get credit for sales.

must_reads.title: Instagram offers to pay creators for long-form content
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Meta is paying creators to post longer videos on Instagram. Platforms competing for creators with cash usually also tweak what links and outbound traffic they allow, so it's worth watching where link-out rules go next.

must_reads.title: Google AI Mode test groups shopping ads under one Sponsored heading
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google is testing grouping shopping ads under one 'Sponsored' label in AI Mode, with free listings under 'All products'. How AI search lays out products decides which retailer gets the click, and that's the space Geniuslink routes traffic through.

must_reads.title: People Inc. is building custom APIs to make its journalism easier for AI agents to use
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Big publishers like People Inc. and Forbes are rebuilding their content so AI agents can read it directly. Many of these publishers earn from affiliate links, so if agents read the content instead of people, the clicks that pay them may shrink.
